notes.title: Dev Update 3
notes.notes:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45517178/08e2cdd294c04475b0d100a5375e28e0b90dd55d.png
Hello, Deminers!
It's been a while since the last Dev Update and since the project is undergoing some major structural changes - its time.

The less fun news:
I've been developing this game and pumping out updates over the last 1.5 years to get as far through the backlog as possible before running out of resources.. And regretfully..

..That time has sadly come, and I gotta to do a job on the side to be able to sustain development costs and all else as only doing this is completely unsustainable.

However..! Everything has secretly been going exactly according to plan as I've managed to get so much in place during this crucial period that I'm confident that this wont impact the full-release date for the game (Q2 2026) at all. Updates will be coming it more slowly, but be more substantial leading up to the full release.

What's next:

Graphical Overhaul
In the next update, a complete graphical overhaul I've been cooking for up for a good while will be deployed. This overhaul completely changes the feel of the game (in the good way). You will have:

 Increased view distances
 Higher texture resolutions
 High quality shadows
 More colors
 More details..
At the cost of... 15% LESS!? computing power than before. 

Not only that... But with this tech, the game will also finally be able to support full day-time which not only looks awesome, but will make the transition into nights feel much more tangible/serious.

A little sneak peak of the environment during daytime using the new pipeline:
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45517178/e1447482442b9d5f2a11737b89a28e9822abc9af.png"]
Gameplay Loop Re-DesignWith all the new features in place, the original vision for the game loop doesn't really hold up anymore or feel obvious at all. 
I'm not super hyped about there being so much in the game but so little incentive or direction for actually doing these things. I can't say for sure exactly how the game loop is going to change just yet, but there will be much more incentive for taking risks and doing different activities around the world so that making the most out of every day is back to being a clear central part of the game. 

Custom Game SettingsThe final thing being added in the upcoming update is a way for the host to customize game settings in the lobby. Most aspects of the game will be tweakable this way like:

 In-Game time speed
 Amount of hours until dusk/nightfall happens
 Mine difficulty scaling
 Player statuses
 Buff durations and values
 Amount of ruins that can spawn individually for each sector
 Maximum ruins depth individually for each sector
 Material costs
 Item costs
 Spawn rates for every enemy
 Etc.. Etc..
 Tweaking anything with this feature disables certain achievements in the game from being attained on that save file, but the replayability it adds to the game is priceless. 

That's all i got for now. I thank you all who have been supporting and believing in my game during these somewhat messy early-access times. ːsteamhappyː

notes.title: Dev Update 2
notes.notes:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45517178/9bef82051421c36f2e09986eaccaedd17cc80dc6.png

Hello Again! ːsteamhappyː 
Here's another roundup of the latest notable changes and additions to Demining.

These weeks have been busy. I've visually reworked the market, made the ATV fully compatible in multiplayer but these are the most...
Standout Improvements / Changes / Additions

Achievements!
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45517178/c1495f1fec89298071e48a3d6a45d8171f0701ca.png{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45517178/cfd118fd20d2b715c1945d5b58e7b31bda0f9a86.png{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45517178/061d7c16682736a670f094f0d6a68f7807833e99.png
Achievements were supposed to be in the game on release but some other more pressing issues came in the way. Now i'm happy to announce that there are 18 achievements up for grabs, where some may provide hints about content you have yet to discover. 

Overworld Changes
The large open tent in lowlands used to serve a purpose in an earlier unreleased version of the game. However, that purpose doesn't exist anymore and it felt like to me that it was only standing in the way for players that wanted to utilize the ATV. I also been meaning to add more dense vegetation to the game so kind of took out two birds with one stone here.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45517178/6aa85d819ed4201231ca786b20ae7f6b6fcb7136.png

While at it, I also made the decision to close down the well for now as it similarly to the Lowlands tent mentioned above - has lost its purpose over time. For now, I've added a lid on top of the well which I intend to turn into a puzzle in the future as may be slightly hinted on the model for it. 

The artifact that could previously be found in the well under certain conditions, can now instead be found on top of the lid if those conditions are met so you don't have to go down to fetch it anymore, for now.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45517178/b8d2a3b99edfdcd4e136255678b3623f83e73261.png

Lastly, random scenic objects now appears in each sector for each day, which is part of some ongoing work to keep the experience fresh for each new day. The pool of objects that can spawn are partly the same objects which a Mimic can hide under so you can never be truly sure of what you think is a mimic anymore unless you see it twitching.

New Hallucination
Initially the game had 3 hallucinations, where one was scrapped right before launch which kind of left the system feel a bit empty. This guy was initially going to be another "Turtle", but one thing led to another. This new hallucination can approach several players at once and also overlap with other active hallucinations. Once he's latched onto a player, he will always follow them around but very slowly for the rest of the day unless its baited into a Spotlight. 

So be sure to keep your sanity high!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45517178/ebb3e462dd21c4bc2e440400d03153805bd315fb.gif

Reworked the disarming section of the tutorial.
Previously, there were always 5 mines to disarm in the tutorials that could be disarmed by anyone. Meaning that if 1 player disarmed all 5 mines, the other 3 players would be left with none. To address this - There are now several "disarm chambers" that will open up when getting to that part of the tutorial. Each chamber has 4 mines to disarm and is individually assigned to players in the game. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45517178/796789200d02f2a4e7d7ca996cd4610462025eac.png

About the frequent/daily patches...
This is not sustainable for my health. Now that the game runs well, most obvious bugs are fixed and many QOL features are implemented I will slow down on the updating. I will instead update the game only when there is a substantial amount of new/changed content. 
If there are any game breaking or soft locking issues I will still hot-fix it on the current version, but hold back on releasing the new stuff til its spicy enough.

This is both for my sake but also to make sure that returning deminers feel like its worth checking out/coming back for.


That's all I got for now.

Thank you for readingːsteamhappyː

notes.title: Dev Update 1
notes.notes:
Hello!ːsteamhappyː
To better include everyone who's been following or trying out the game, I’ll be sharing occasional summaries highlighting notable changes, improvements, and what’s currently in the works. These updates are meant to keep you in the loop and give some insight into the development process as it evolves.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45517178/8facd385556933ecdf0e89ba82ae60e5e41f7cbd.png

In hindsight, the initial version of the game had some serious issues in terms of optimization, explanation of game mechanics or presentation in general. 
I've never published a game before and the initial build clearly lacked the quality I truly believed I would have time to sort out before the game inevitably came out.

Among a plethora of bug fixes and QOL-Improvements in all regards, these are the...
Standout Improvements / Changes:

 Reworked how static objects and lightning is rendered in the game.
While strong systems didn't experience GPU/CPU spikes to the same extent, if you were hovering around the minimum requirements to run the game - It was awful for no good reason. 
Obviously, there was a reason and it has been massively improved since. I will still keep looking for ways to improve the performance of the game and passively send out updates in this regard in coming patches but the improvements made can be clearly felt in-game and seen when monitoring your cpu/gpu which is great.

 Completely scrapped the previous tutorial and replaced it with a brand new (optional) introductory area.
It is safe to say that the initial tutorial was horrible. Pretty much every player I saw play the game during the first week struggled with understanding the fundamentals of the game. Being dropped into the game right away with several different interactables and a wall of text covering half your screen was not the way - So I completely deleted it and reworked the new player-experience from scratch. There will still be patches made to the new and improved tutorial, even though its much better than before it still contains some elements that can be simplified further. The mission to not overwhelm new players continues, but its much more digestable now.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45517178/75883d60f87571b95708666a4793a015d6ccf6fb.png

  Labyrinth puzzle mechanic when disarming mines removed & replaced
 Another thing i saw players struggle with heavily, has been the maze/labyrinth puzzle when disarming mines. So I reworked the labyrinth puzzle into a new maze-like mechanic that is more fair, visually satisfying, varying and most importantly self-explanatory.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45517178/f0de08f613e9b7c02ab2231f8c9d7b11daa39cd4.png

Upcoming:
 ATV improvements and changes
 The ATV was a heavily experimental feature added to the game a bit too close to the release which is why its limited to one zone only but it's very clear to me at this point that the ATV is a fun addition for players and its here to stay. 
The ATV will see improvements in terms of smoothness for clients(those who aren't hosting a session), more dynamic/realistic steering, a much larger fuel pool and also being able to access more areas with it. 
Another goal that I aim to implement is the ability to store items in the ATV, so you can stash treasures in it for an example, allowing you drive around and plunder as many ruins as you want without having to return to camp.

 Enemy Improvements
While they work fine mostly, I want all enemies to have much more distinctive/noticeable behaviors.
For an example: all enemies currently have wildly different behaviors depending on if they are encountered in the Overworld or inside of a Ruin and also if they spawn as a reaction to a siren going off or what time it is. 
I'm quite certain this goes completely unnoticed, especially for new players or players that doesn't spend some time within the game so the presentation there is definitely lacking. 
So to summarize, there will be improvements in terms of visual feedback, sounds, and in some cases changes to the enemy models depending on the conditions mentioned above to clarify exactly what you're dealing with.

  Market UI Rework
The Market UI will be reworked to be less confusing, with the buying of items and selling of materials being completely separated into different tabs. General facelift incoming.

That's all I got for now *tips fedora*
Thanks for reading!ːsteamhappyː
